name: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS)
summary: The carpal tunnel is a passage at the front of the wrist formed by the carpal bones and the transverse carpal ligament. The median nerve and nine flexor tendons pass through it.

looksLike: Tingling and numbness in the thumb, index, middle and half of the ring finger.
Worse at night, waking the patient; shaking the hand relieves it ("flick sign").
Worse with driving, holding a phone, prolonged gripping.

Later: clumsiness, dropping objects, weak thumb abduction, wasting of the thenar eminence (base of thumb). The palm is usually spared, because the palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve passes above the tunnel.
redFlags: Sudden severe symptoms after wrist trauma or fracture
Bilateral hand clumsiness with gait change
firstSteps: Mild to moderate (intermittent symptoms, no wasting): conservative care for about 6 to 12 weeks.
Severe (constant numbness, wasting) or failed conservative care: refer for nerve studies and surgical opinion.

assess: Sensation: thumb, index, middle finger tips versus little finger, and the palm.
Strength: abductor pollicis brevis (thumb lifted at right angles to the palm against resistance).
Optional: a validated symptom questionnaire (Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire).

blocks.text: The carpal tunnel is a passage at the front of the wrist formed by the carpal bones and the transverse carpal ligament. The median nerve and nine flexor tendons pass through it. Increased pressure in the tunnel compresses the median nerve. CTS is the most common nerve entrapment. Risk factors include female sex, pregnancy, diabetes, hypothyroidism, rheumatoid arthritis, obesity, and repetitive forceful wrist use [Ref – to verify].

blocks.text: E3. Tinel sign at the wrist
Tap over the median nerve at the carpal tunnel. Tingling into the median fingers is positive. Accuracy is variable [Ref – to verify].
The patient shades symptom areas on a hand diagram. A "classic" or "probable" pattern supports CTS [Ref – to verify].

steps: **Median paraesthesia, night symptoms, positive compression or Phalen, normal neck exam:** working diagnosis CTS.
**Mild to moderate (intermittent symptoms, no wasting):** conservative care for about 6 to 12 weeks.
**Severe (constant numbness, wasting) or failed conservative care:** refer for nerve studies and surgical opinion.

Straight hand, hook fist, full fist, tabletop, straight fist

Neutral wrist, breaks from forceful gripping, larger tool handles

blocks.text: Splinting is the best supported conservative treatment [Ref – to verify]. Ultrasound and laser: evidence weak or inconsistent; not routinely recommended. Corticosteroid injection by a doctor may give short- to medium-term relief.

sections.title: L to M. Management and reassessment

blocks.text: Track Boston questionnaire, night waking frequency, two-point discrimination, thumb abduction strength. After surgery: early finger movement, scar care, gradual grip loading from about 2 to 4 weeks as advised.

blocks.label: CLINICAL CASE
body: A 45-year-old woman with diabetes wakes 3 times a night with numb thumb, index and middle fingers, relieved by shaking her hand. Carpal compression test reproduces symptoms at 15 seconds. Neck exam normal. No wasting. Working diagnosis: mild to moderate CTS. Plan: night splint, tendon and nerve gliding, ergonomic advice, encourage diabetes control through her doctor, reassess at 6 weeks.

items: **Why is the palm usually spared?** The palmar cutaneous branch leaves the median nerve before the tunnel.
**What finding makes surgery referral urgent?** Thenar wasting or constant numbness.
**Which conservative treatment has the best support?** Night splinting in neutral.
**How do you separate CTS from C6 radiculopathy?** Neck findings, reflex changes and a root pattern versus night symptoms and wrist provocation.
**Why ask about diabetes and thyroid?** They increase risk and need medical management.
